title: Ordinary counit square under the first-factor unit
statement: Let $R,A,B,A_q,D$ be commutative rings with $R$-algebra structures on $A,B,A_q$, a compatible $A$-algebra structure on $A_q$, and $(A\otimes_R B)$- and $(A_q\otimes_R B)$-algebra structures on $D$. Fix derived categories of $R$- and $B$-modules. For an $A$-module cochain complex $Q$, take models $L,K$ of its base-derived tensor cohomology and that of $A_q\otimes_A Q$, respectively [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model]. Let $u:Q_R\to(A_q\otimes_A Q)_R$ be the unit $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, and let $c$ be the induced derived cohomology map [lem-pc-first-localization-map]. Put $X=(A\otimes_R B)\otimes_A Q$ and $Y=(A_q\otimes_R B)\otimes_{A_q}(A_q\otimes_A Q)$. The additive chain map $\phi:X_{\mathrm{ab}}\to Y_{\mathrm{ab}}$ is obtained by $L.ordinaryIso^{-1}$, $B\otimes_R u$, and $K.ordinaryIso$. For every $i\in\mathbf Z$, the ordinary comparison maps satisfy $U_E(L.comparison_i);s_X^{-1};H^i(\phi)=U_B(c);U_F(K.comparison_i);s_Y^{-1}$, where $E=A\otimes_R B$, $F=A_q\otimes_R B$, $U$ forgets scalars and $s_X:H^i(X_{\mathrm{ab}})\simeq U_E H^i(X)$ and $s_Y$ are the canonical exact-functor homology isomorphisms. No coefficient compatibility in $D$, localization hypothesis, or isomorphism assumption on the comparisons is required.

proof.text: Install L.universal and K.universal. The canonical leftDerivedNatIso intertwines the counits by leftDerivedNatTrans_fac. Combine this identity with naturality of L.counit on the image of firstLocalizationUnit in the homotopy category, and apply the derived homology functor.

Substitute comparison_eq for both models and unfold firstLocalizationCohomologyMap. Cancel the adjacent ordinaryIso homology maps. Naturality of derived and homotopy homology factorization isomorphisms turns the counit identity into the B-linear ordinary square.

Prove that the homology isomorphism for forgetting after scalar restriction equals the direct forgetting isomorphism: cancel the mapped homology projection, use its compatibility with mapHomologyIso, then cancel the cycles inclusion and use mapCyclesIso_hom_iCycles. Taking inverses transports both comparisons to additive groups.

Forget the B-linear square, compose with the inverse homology-forgetting isomorphism of the target, and use mapHomologyIso_inv_naturality for the ordinary chain map. The transported comparisons are exactly the displayed additive square.

lean.statement:
theorem firstLocalization_ordinary_square (i : ℤ)
    (Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
    (L : ModuleCat.BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R A B Q D)
    (K : ModuleCat.BaseDerivedTensorCohomologyModel R Aq B ((extend A Aq).obj Q) D) :
    (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⊗[R] B)) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).map (L.comparison i) ≫
      (((((ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap A (A ⊗[R] B))).mapHomologicalComplex
        (.up ℤ)).obj Q).sc i).mapHomologyIso
          (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} (A ⊗[R] B)) AddCommGrpCat.{u})).inv ≫
      HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
        (((forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} B) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map
          (L.ordinaryIso.inv ≫ ((ModuleCat.extendScalars
            (algebraMap R B)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map (firstLocalizationUnit R A Aq Q) ≫
              K.ordinaryIso.hom)) i =
    (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} B) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).map
      (firstLocalizationCohomologyMap R A Aq B D Q L K i) ≫
      (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} (Aq ⊗[R] B)) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).map (K.comparison i) ≫
        (((((ModuleCat.extendScalars (algebraMap Aq (Aq ⊗[R] B))).mapHomologicalComplex
          (.up ℤ)).obj ((extend A Aq).obj Q)).sc i).mapHomologyIso
            (forget₂ (ModuleCat.{u} (Aq ⊗[R] B)) AddCommGrpCat.{u})).inv
